title: English for HR Management
overview: English for HR Management is a practical, workplace-focused language program designed to strengthen the communication skills required across the employee lifecycle. Participants develop the vocabulary, accuracy, fluency and professional tone needed to manage recruitment, onboarding, performance discussions, employee relations, learning and development, HR reporting and sensitive workplace conversations in English. The course combines authentic HR documents, realistic conversations and task-based practice to improve both spoken and written communication.
audience: Human resources officers, coordinators, specialists and generalists.
Recruitment, talent acquisition and onboarding professionals.
Learning and development, employee engagement and performance management staff.
HR administrators, payroll coordinators and employee relations personnel.
Supervisors and managers who regularly communicate HR matters in English.
methodology: Facilitated language practice using HR scenarios; guided vocabulary and grammar activities; recruitment and appraisal role-plays; email, policy and report-writing workshops; listening exercises based on meetings and interviews; peer feedback; simulated HR conversations; and practical formative assessments. Activities are adjusted to participants’ starting English proficiency.
competencies: Accurate use of HR terminology and professional workplace expressions.
Clear and appropriate HR emails, notices, letters and short reports.
Confident interviewing, questioning, listening and clarification skills.
Professional communication in performance and employee relations discussions.
Effective explanation of policies, procedures and employment-related information.
Confidentiality-aware, culturally sensitive and tactful communication.
objectives: Use essential HR terminology accurately in spoken and written English.
Write clear recruitment messages, HR emails, meeting notes and employee communications.
Conduct and participate in job interviews and onboarding conversations.
Explain HR policies, benefits, leave arrangements and workplace procedures clearly.
Structure performance feedback and development discussions using professional language.
Handle sensitive employee questions and difficult conversations with empathy and discretion.
Read and summarize common HR documents, dashboards and reports.
Deliver short HR briefings and present people-related information confidently.
